# Thakeen / Nashr — Development Log

**Period:** 2026-09-17 (first commit) to 2026-10-12 (collection ended 2026-10-12 about 16:30 UTC). **Repository:** `iAbulkhair/Nashr`. **Times are UTC** unless a source gave none (then the time is the earliest commit/message in the cluster).

This is a log, not a summary. Every entry says what was known, what was decided and why, what was done (commits, PRs, branches), what went wrong, how it was corrected, and what the founder said. Where the sources do not record a reason or a time, the entry says `unknown` or `reason not recorded` instead of guessing.

## How to read it

- Entries are chronological: `## date`, then `### HH:MM UTC — title (eNNN)`. Each has a **Type** line with tags: `action`, `founder`, `rule`, `error`, `decision`, `correction`, `merge`, `planning`, `ci`, `security`, `docs`, `design`, `research`, `deploy`, `incident`, `branch`.
- `(inferred)` marks a statement that is not stated in any source but follows from them.
- Founder quotes are verbatim, in the language they were written in. Founder: أبوالخير.
- Appendices: [A branch ledger](#appendix-a--branch-ledger) · [B PR ledger](#appendix-b--pr-ledger) · [C mistakes and lessons](#appendix-c--mistakes--lessons-index) · [D founder instructions](#appendix-d--founder-instructions--corrections-index) · [E sources and gaps](#appendix-e--sources-method-and-gaps).

## Scale

- 755 log entries over 20 calendar days with activity; 1104 commits (`git log --all`, collected in two passes: 2026-10-10 for the period up to 11:40 UTC and 2026-10-12 about 16:30 UTC for the rest; later commits are not in the log), 157 pull requests (140 merged, 3 closed unmerged), 290 branches (remote and local-only), 161 Claude sessions on this machine at the first collection (2026-10-10; not recounted in the second pass).

# Timeline


<a id="2026-09-17"></a>
## 2026-09-17
> Day 0: in one long session (about 13 hours, one Claude Code session with two context compactions, model Claude Fable 5.1) the founder went from "copy Enrich Labs for the Gulf" to a live Arabic/English marketing site, a working multi-agent SaaS v0 on Vercel + Upstash + Anthropic, 7 named agents, evals, admin console and design system, all pushed straight to `main` with no tests, no CI and no pull requests.

<a id="e001"></a>
### 07:54 UTC — Session opens with a research pass on Enrich Labs (e001)

- **Type:** research, planning, founder
- **Context / Thinking:** The founder asked how to copy the business model of enrichlabs.ai (Helena, an autonomous AI marketing agent) for the GCC. The very first message is not in the dossier; the later compaction summary records it as "how to copy enrichlabs.ai's business model for the GCC". The session started in a scratch workspace with no project folder.
- **Decision:** Assistant framed it as "copy the model, not the brand": subscription plus credits, 3-day trial, agent that plans and does the work, human approves. Own name, own copy, own design. Why a GCC version can win: Helena is built for the US stack (Arabic, Hijri/Gulf seasons, Salla/Zid, WhatsApp, Snap are missing). Enrich facts recorded: plans Starter $39/200 credits, Pro $99/700, Pro Plus $199/2000, Enterprise custom; 1 credit = post/image/ad, 2 = blog post, 12 = 4-12s video; Miami, ~5 people, founded 2024.
- **Action:** Web search and fetch only. No code. 07:57 founder switched the session model with `/model claude-fable-5-1` (all day-0 commits carry "Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1").
- **Outcome / state:** A comparison table and GCC plan were on screen; no repo existed yet.

<a id="e002"></a>
### 07:58 UTC — Four scoping decisions: brand, language, niche, hosting (e002)

- **Type:** decision, founder, planning
- **Context / Thinking:** Founder instruction: build the site, publish it, then the full PRD, a financial model in XLSX and a pitch deck. A brainstorming skill with a hard "approval before implementation" gate was loaded, so the assistant classified the request as architectural and asked four questions (AskUserQuestion, answered 08:03).
- **Decision:** Brand = Nashr (نشر), persona Noor (نور), recommended option taken; rejected Rawaj (رواج, persona Sara) and Tarweej (ترويج, persona Layla). Language = Arabic default (RTL) + English toggle; English-only and Arabic-only rejected. Niche: the founder rejected the recommended beachhead (Salla/Zid e-commerce) and chose "All + legal firms, startups, shopify and real-estate developers". Hosting: the founder rejected the recommended Claude Artifact and chose Vercel (real deploy, custom domain possible).
- **Action:** Assistant then presented a four-deliverable design (site, PRD, 36-month XLSX model with live formulas, 14-slide deck) at 08:03 and started building at 08:06.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The founder said Vercel was installed; the assistant found no binary and no `~/.vercel` auth and installed it itself (device-flow login at 08:28-08:34). Reason for the mismatch not recorded.
- **Founder:** 08:06 "files not open / vercel is installed"
- **Outcome / state:** Scope fixed: all niches (the "beachhead" focus the assistant recommended was overridden; the founder's later 20:02 answer repeats "all").

<a id="e017"></a>
### 12:06 UTC — Connector framework with encrypted token storage (e017)

- **Type:** action, deploy, security
- **Context / Thinking:** Founder "build connectors".
- **Decision:** One framework for OAuth and key-based providers; tokens AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest with `CONNECT_SECRET`, never returned by any API, deleted on disconnect; WordPress publishes as draft (safe default).
- **Action:** commit `99f233e9` (12:12): WordPress, WooCommerce, Klaviyo live (customers paste their own keys); X (PKCE), Shopify, Google, Meta, Salla, Zid, LinkedIn, TikTok, Snapchat wired but dormant until env keys exist; publish buttons in inbox and chat tool; privacy and terms pages `/ar/privacy`, `/ar/terms`.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The assistant's local mock-WordPress test used `localhost:3999` which the code normalized to https and failed; test rerun with explicit http, then deployed (a test artifact, not a code bug).
- **Founder:** 12:06 "build connectors"
- **Outcome / state:** 12 providers (3 live, 9 waiting on keys). Later (18 Sep) audit found OAuth return not session-bound and Shopify without HMAC; connectors were dormant so not exploitable yet.

<a id="e018"></a>
### 12:17 UTC — "Did you add all connectors?" and the Enrich GTM copy (e018)

- **Type:** founder, research, action, deploy
- **Context / Thinking:** Founder asked two things: did all connectors get added, and "deep search, analyze, build and copy all their GTM and marketing activities" (he learned of Enrich through its mailing list).

<a id="e095"></a>
### 14:19 UTC — P0 credit bypass: `"constructor" in TASK_COST` reproduced live and fixed (e095)

- **Type:** security, incident, action
- **Context / Thinking:** The assistant refused to repeat the P0 from the audit until it had reproduced it, then exploited it on a running server before touching code. `if (!(type in TASK_COST))` walks the prototype chain, so `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty` and `__proto__` passed; `TASK_COST[type]` was a function, every comparison against `NaN` was false, and `u.credits < cost` was false at a zero balance.
- **Decision:** Fix the guard at every call site and repair the ledger, and prove it over HTTP before and after.
- **Action:** Exploit: `POST /api/generate {"type":"constructor"}` answered 200 and the balance went 50 to `null`. On the memory store the balance is literally `NaN`, so the next call generated ten items for free; on Upstash the value round-trips as `null`, which blocks the owner's own calls while the attack path still passes. `gov.autoApprove["constructor"]` was also truthy, so items were written `approved`, bypassing the inbox that publishing depends on. Same hole in `/api/mcp`, in `/api/admin/plan` (`b.plan in PLAN_CREDITS`), and the chat tools `generate_content` and `draft_items` had no guard at all. Added `isTaskType` and `isPlan` in `src/lib/tasks.ts`, shaped like `isAgentId`; `charge()` and `adjust()` now refuse a non-finite cost and repair a damaged balance. After: all five keys answer `400 bad_type`, balance stays 50, a legitimate call creates 10 and leaves 40.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The original audit statement understated it: the follow-up call was free and unlimited, not just a bricked account. Verification was first attempted against a stale server and a throttled signup (14:19:31 and 14:19:43) and had to be redone on a fresh server.
- **Correction:** Pinned by 4 Playwright API tests plus `tests/type-guards.test.ts`; committed as `f023179c` (14:49).
- **Founder:** None in this step.
- **Outcome / state:** P0 closed, verified live, pinned. Later extended: `7753c181` (17:56) repaired the NaN-repair write-back.

<a id="e114"></a>
### 19:11 UTC — CI goes red: 40 mobile-safari tests bounce to login; root cause is a Secure cookie on plain http (e114)

- **Type:** incident, ci, error, security
- **Context / Thinking:** The first full CI run, now with E2E (commit `2ebbcbc`), failed 40 tests, all in mobile-safari and all "renders for a signed-in owner". Locally the same tests passed on both projects, four clean runs.
- **Decision:** Fix the cause rather than the symptom: all five session cookies were marked `Secure` when `NODE_ENV === "production"`, which describes the build and not how the response travels. A `Secure` cookie sent over plain http is discarded by a conforming client and the next request carries no cookie, with no error anywhere.
- **Action:** `399ee171` (19:16): one `sessionCookie()` for all five call sites; `Secure` unless plain http to the loopback interface; a real host over http keeps `Secure` and refuses to work (loud failure on purpose); `localhost.evil.example` is not loopback. Verified against a running production build: loopback http emits no `Secure`, `x-forwarded-proto: https` emits it, a real host over http emits it. At 19:17 a CI-monitor event reported "Nashr CI" failing; it was the cancelled run of the previous commit, killed by `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The failure could not be reproduced locally (WebKit on macOS stores the cookie); the assistant verified the `Set-Cookie` header directly. The Auto-fix event at 19:17 was a false alarm; changing code for it would have been chasing a phantom.
- **Correction:** The assistant noted that every push during a run produces this noise.
- **Founder:** None in this step.
- **Outcome / state:** Anyone self-hosting over http would never have been able to log in; production on Vercel (always https) was unchanged. Also noted: the out-of-scope CI commit caught this bug.

### 10:00 UTC — PR #197: secure the connector OAuth flow before any platform key reaches production (e143)

- **Type:** security, action, merge, rule
- **Context / Thinking:** The owner was registering the platform apps now (X, Shopify, Meta, Salla, Zid and the rest) on `nashr-tau.vercel.app`, so five known gaps in the connect flow (open since the 22 Sep review) go live the moment the first client id is set in production.

Session binding (#37): start route stores the state in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie scoped to `/api/connect`; the callback clears it and refuses (`session_mismatch`) before any code exchange unless the cookie matches the state and the signed-in account owns the state's workspace. Provider binding (#38): a state completes only its provider. Shopify host (#39): single-label `*.myshopify.com` only, 400 before redirect. Shopify HMAC (#113): callback verifies the HMAC over the query and requires the shop the flow started for; the fallback to the unsigned query `shop` is gone. Token refresh (#34): `getFreshConnection` refreshes a token expiring within 5 minutes under a per-connection lock (X rotates single-use refresh tokens) and keeps the rotated token; a refused refresh or 401/403 marks `needsReconnect` and the Integrations page shows a Reconnect button. Rules 67-70 in `tests/oauth-connect.test.ts` (9 cases; the five callback cases fail on the old callback). `flows.md` section 11, `permissions.md` row 46, `tests.md` updated.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The five gaps themselves: a leaked state could attach someone else's platform account to a customer's workspace; an X state could complete the LinkedIn callback; Shopify start redirected to any host; no HMAC check; X refresh token not rotated.
- **Correction:** this PR.
- **Outcome / state:** Safe to add platform client ids. Variable and permission docs updated in the same commit per CLAUDE.md.

### 19:13 UTC — Reem review fixes, including an MCP link-hijack security bug (e209)

- **Type:** security, correction, action
- **Context / Thinking:** A review of Reem phase 1 found a security hole: an MCP client could close any open item by moving its link onto an already-approved inbox item (`todo_update {id, task_id}` then `agenda_get`), because the MCP route does not validate arguments against the tool schema. Other findings: idle scopes never purged, a proposal on a snoozed item stayed hidden, restore did not count against the 500 open-item limit, agents were never told today's date, copy promised a timed reminder phase 1 cannot deliver.
- **Decision:** `toolFields` reads `task_id` for `todo_create` only; `mutateItem` refuses link changes from anyone but the owner on the web (`owner_only`); chat and MCP may link only at creation and only to a pending task (`link_not_pending`); every agent prompt starts with `NOW (Riyadh, UTC+3)`; copy says «سجّل عليّ» and "In the morning brief and alerts", never a reminder at a set time.
- **Action:** `cb2cf025` (19:13). Rules 157-160, 162, 165, 167, 169-171 extended and 172-174 added; each fix checked by reverting it (22 reverts).
- **Errors & mistakes:** The shipped phase 1 draft contained the link-hijack hole and a promise the product could not keep.
- **Correction:** Fixed in `cb2cf025` before the PR opened.
- **Outcome / state:** Branch reviewed; Taskuary fixes next.

### 16:01 UTC — One-time mails marked sent only after Resend accepts; burned markers repaired (e259)

- **Type:** security, action, error, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** The signup nudge and lifecycle notes claimed their 400-day marker before sending. Since `RESEND_API_KEY` arrived on 2026-09-18 every send was refused for lack of `MAIL_FROM`, yet recorded as done and never retried: 13 days of one-time mail lost.
- **Decision:** Claim-then-confirm: `sendOnce` takes a 120 s claim, writes the marker only when the send answered true, and the nudge and lifecycle are gated on `mailReady()` (key and `MAIL_FROM`). Repair old markers once. Alternative not taken: re-send to everyone without a cutoff, which would mail some customers twice.
- **Action:** `0b7baf0d` at 16:01 (rules 350-352, `tests/mail-once.test.ts`); `fd007204` at 17:25 (markers now a dated `{ sent }` record; old-guard marker cleared once behind a 400-day `notifyrepair:` flag; rules 363-365); `b1fa52c8` at 17:26 (docs, the founder's yes recorded); `0dbc1a43` at 17:42 (`REPAIR_BEFORE` 2026-10-01 17:00 UTC, write time read from the remaining TTL, rule 367).
- **Errors & mistakes:** `0b7baf0d` body: "every send Resend refused while MAIL_FROM is unset was recorded as done and never retried". `0dbc1a43` found a second hole in the repair: main still ran the old guard, so markers written after `MAIL_FROM` went live would have stood for successful sends and been mailed twice.
- **Correction:** Cutoff independent of deploy order (`0dbc1a43`).

<a id="e260"></a>
### 16:01 UTC — Founder console: server-side key sessions, no default founder email, 15 minutes idle (e260)

- **Type:** security, rule, decision
- **Context / Thinking:** #35: the key form put `WAITLIST_ADMIN_KEY` itself in the `nashr_admin` cookie for 30 days and logout only deleted the cookie. #36: `adminEmails()` fell back to a personal address in source.
- **Decision:** A right key (`sameSecret`) opens a key session: cookie holds a random 32-byte id, the record `adminsession:{sha256(id)}` holds a key fingerprint; logout deletes the record, rotating the key ends all, unsetting disables the path. No email fallback: with `ADMIN_EMAILS` unset nobody is a founder, so `ADMIN_EMAILS` must be set in production before shipping. Founder decision of 17:14: 15 minutes idle, 12 hours at most.
- **Action:** `eeb73b8a` at 16:01 (rules 310-315, later 420-424); `1caa7d93` at 17:19 (`ADMIN_SESSION_IDLE`, `ADMIN_SESSION_MAX`, renewal at most once a minute with `SET XX EX`; rules 312 rewritten, 325 new); `ae3bf424` at 17:28 (customer-view work counts as activity; the console says when the session ended through `adminFetch`).

- **Correction:** `ae3bf424`, rule 325 rewritten.
- **Founder:** 17:14 «٨. ربع ساعة».
- **Outcome / state:** In #233 (merged 19:52). `ADMIN_EMAILS` was added in Vercel at 19:26.

### 20:11 UTC — Task 4: one chase rule for quiet days, Ramadan hours and absences (rules 475-477); ruling R10 (e310)

- **Type:** action, rule, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** Task 4 was dispatched at 19:55 on Opus with rulings R1, R2, R5 and R7. `chaseMoment(item, now, cal, away)` decides when the owner may chase someone:
  - Agents' items never move.
  - An away contact is chased after the absence.
  - Quiet days move a chase to briefAt on the next working day.
  - Ramadan's off-hours move it to the next window start.
  - An already chaseable debt waits while today is not a working moment.

### 14:13 UTC — Task 5 (Opus): spawn the next copy on every close path; race review and repair path (e337)

- **Type:** action, rule, error, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** The dangerous part of recurring items is opening the next copy exactly once. Four close paths (complete, confirm_done, skip, linked close) must each open the next copy through one claim, and a retried close must finish a half-done spawn.
- **Decision:** `spawnNext` claims `sec:spawn` with SET NX (2 days), writes round 1 the closed copy with `nextId` and the close audit, round 2 the new copy and a `spawn` line by the rule (R51). Reopen deletes an untouched next copy under its own lock, keeps an edited one with the `two_open` note, and answers 503 when that lock or read fails. The implementer's judgement calls (a 7th `line` parameter, repair answering 200 before `expectRev`, `deleteNextCopy` doing its own soft-delete) were put to an Opus reviewer, who passed the spec (R32-R35, R39, R41, R48, R49, R51, R52).
- **Action:** `8053f177` (14:13, rules 497-499, 2162 tests); review at 14:17; `d0c7a3aa` (14:21, repair soft-deleted next copy, pin count end and open-cap skip, 2165 tests, three new tests, rows 497-499 reworded so they claim no more than the tests cover).
- **Errors & mistakes:** The reviewer's one Important finding: a series can stop silently if round 2 fails and the owner never retries the close (R51 is not self-healing). Also a soft-deleted claimed `nextId` was not treated as missing, so a repair would have left the series stuck. The assistant ruled the first as an accepted risk: a daily repair sweep was left out of A2 because the case needs a Redis failure between two consecutive writes (flagged in the final "Rulings I made" list for the founder).
- **Correction:** `d0c7a3aa` handles the soft-deleted `nextId`; two rare cases were accepted as owner-only and visible: restoring a deliberately deleted next copy, and reviving an ended series with an old close. A re-review of the fix round was skipped (three tests and a helper, and the failing test was shown red first); the final whole-branch review covered it.
- **Founder:** none.
- **Outcome / state:** Core spawn engine in place at 2165 tests.

<a id="e339"></a>
### 14:48 UTC — Task 7 (Opus): warn then purge closed copies; adversarial review of data deletion (e339)

- **Type:** action, security, rule, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** This is the only task that deletes customer data. The base rule loaded on the implementer: never delete a copy without a warning at least seven days earlier, never delete a series kept by the Keep switch, never delete a copy that was reopened between the read and the delete.
- **Decision:** `warnSeries` moves sdone to spurge and sends one notification per brand and local day naming at most five series, with a 30-day marker (R44); `purgeSeries` re-reads each copy and its spurge score under the item lock before deleting; `requeueSeries` repairs (R50); `setSeriesKeep` has a `keep_limit` 409 at 500. Reviewer (Opus) accepted three deviations: the marker is written with SET (not SETNX), un-keep and keep clear the marker so a new naming warning is forced, and the warning email is sent unless the account preference is "none". The uncapped daily sweep was a further point put to the reviewer and left as a minor.
- **Action:** `8891ade0` (14:48, rules 502-505, new `src/lib/secretary-series.ts`, `db` gains `zscore`, cron outcome adds `{warned}w{deleted}d`, 2194 tests); review 14:54; `5c23f82c` (14:56, 2198 tests).
- **Errors & mistakes:** Important: one per-item throw rejected the whole purge, so deletions already made were missing from the count and from the audit line. Also a restored copy could be deleted before seven days from its restore time, and un-keep left pending purge entries so deletion could happen without a fresh warning.
- **Correction:** `5c23f82c`: each copy runs through its own try/catch and a failed copy stays in `spurge` for the next day; floor of now plus seven days for moved or restored copies; un-keep clears spurge; ids filtered before MGET. Left without a fix and written to the ledger as minors: the warning count undercounts above 200 copies, a skipped id stays in `sdone`, the `w` counter mixes silent and named moves, and the uncapped daily sweep needs a cap or weekly schedule if series reach thousands. The record is deleted first, then the index removals are caught; the final review had to confirm every reader of the indexes ignores a dead id.
- **Founder:** none.
- **Outcome / state:** Deletion path guarded and tested; no customer data deleted in production yet (code not merged).

<a id="e372"></a>
### 07:22 UTC — B1 design proposal: secret token in the URL path as a named exception (e372)

- **Type:** design, security, decision
- **Context / Thinking:** Calendar apps do not send auth headers, so the secret must sit in the path. The project rule is "secrets are never accepted in URLs", so this is the one documented exception. Assistant created branch `claude/reem-b1-ics-feed` from main and listed rejected alternatives: HMAC without storage (cannot revoke a single link), Basic auth (Google does not support it), OAuth (weeks of verification).
- **Decision:** Random 32-byte token, only its SHA-256 stored (with account, brand, member). Open items with a due date only, title plus contact, never notes (not even private ones), no RRULE (a recurring series shows its open instance, so it stays correct with the Hijri calendar). Narrowing of the exception: read only, bound to one member, not in logs, `no-referrer`, revocable in one click, rate limited, documented in `permissions.md`. Unknown token returns 404 with no distinction. Routes: public `GET /api/secretary/feed/{token}.ics` and `GET/POST/DELETE /api/secretary/feed` for management. Card in the calendar page with copy button, `webcal://` link, renew and stop; full link shown once on creation.
- **Action:** Branch `claude/reem-b1-ics-feed` created. Spec not yet written (waited for the founder's approval of the design).
- **Errors & mistakes:** none.
- **Founder:** none in this entry.
- **Outcome / state:** Design waiting on the founder. The assistant flagged the secret-in-URL exception as "قرار يخصك".

### 15:14 UTC — Store Phase B: twice-daily scheduled sync (PR #267) (e421)

- **Type:** action, rule, deploy
- **Context / Thinking:** Founder asked for Phase B "sync twice a day". Hosting cron limit checked: Vercel allows several schedules per path.
- **Decision:** `GET /api/cron/stores`, cron bearer only (`sameSecret`), two `vercel.json` entries on one path at 02:00 and 14:00 UTC (05:00 and 17:00 Riyadh), each once a day so it works on any plan at no cost. Through `runCronBatch`: one marker per workspace and half-day, six at a time, resumable. Reads only the store the workspace already reports on (or its only connected store); several stores and no snapshot is the owner's choice (button). A snapshot under 10 hours old is left alone. A failed read keeps the last good snapshot and writes `storesyncfail:{scope}` with a status code only (never a platform message or key), shown under the store card; 5xx or network errors retry once from the batch, lost key permission does not. No model call, no credits. Ads stay on the daily cron.
- **Action:** Commit `19fc6077` on branch `claude/stores-scheduled-sync` (15:20), rules 623-627 (`tests/store-scheduled-sync.test.ts`, 18 tests), four system docs and spec updated, `role-gates.test.ts`. `npm run check` 136 files, 3743 tests. ### 19:47 UTC — Composio connect fails on Preview (connect_failed) (e439)

- **Type:** error, incident, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** The founder pasted the integrations screen text "Verification failed. Check the details. (connect_failed)" for Instagram (twice) and LinkedIn (once).
- **Decision:** The assistant found the start route logged only "error" for every SDK failure, hiding the cause. First it added a safe log shape (class names, HTTP status, Composio code; never the message or body), then diagnosed after the next attempt.
- **Action:** `09099c38` "log why a Composio connect fails" (19:52; `errorShape` walks the cause chain, rule 636 then renumbered); `59d224a4` "Composio connect works on Preview" (20:02): the measured run failed because OAuth went through but the first profile read threw `ComposioToolVersionRequiredError` since no toolkit version was pinned (the SDK will not execute on "latest"); the account stayed ACTIVE at Composio so every retry hit `TS-SDK::MULTIPLE_CONNECTED_ACCOUNTS` before the browser left. Fixes: pin a dated version for all 13 toolkits, allow multiple accounts (`allowMultiple`), discard a failed account (`composioDiscard`), and route start redirects back to Thakeen.
- **Errors & mistakes:** At 19:54 the assistant's hypothesis was that the key was created in a project other than Thakeen so it could not see the auth configs; the founder answered «ما فيه الا مشروع ذكين» (there is only the Thakeen project), so the hypothesis was wrong. The log said only "error" for the first two attempts.
- **Correction:** `09099c38` then `59d224a4`; founder retried («جربت») at 19:55.
- **Founder:** 19:47 pasted "Verification failed ... (connect_failed)"; 19:54 «ما فيه الا مشروع ذكين»; 19:55 «جربت»

- **Context / Thinking:** With the webpack build live, `/ar` and `/en` returned 200 and `/` redirected to `/ar`. But the site was running with no environment variables at all. A new build was started to guarantee the app picked it up; the guard was verified at 16:09-16:11 with a read-only request that touches the database, which returned a 500 (the site refused to run without a real database). Pushes to `claude/hostinger-build` redeployed automatically with webpack. The assistant asked the founder to decide the database question (share the existing Upstash database or create a separate one) and listed the env vars and the 8 cron jobs still to add.

Nobody signing up in that window is recorded, but the assistant could not rule it out from its own checks (inferred from its note that "no one can sign up into a temporary store" only after the guard).

### 05:35 UTC — Production guards fire on any host, failing closed (PR #273, PR #274) (e448)

- **Type:** security, rule, action, branch
- **Context / Thinking:** On 2026-10-07 the live site had been protected only by a hand-set `VERCEL_ENV=production`. If anyone replaced the hPanel env vars without that value, rules 430 (never the memory store) and 431 (never the `[DEV MOCK]` model) would silently stop firing and the live site would run on the memory store with mock model output.
- **Decision:** Fail closed on any host. A new `src/lib/deploy-env.ts` `isProductionDeploy()`: `VERCEL_ENV=production` or `APP_ENV=production` means production (not overridable); `APP_ENV` of `test`, `development` or `preview` means not production and any other value, typos included, means production; `VERCEL_ENV` of `preview` or `development` means not production; otherwise `NODE_ENV === "production"` means production. An explicit `APP_ORIGIN` check or explicit `APP_ENV=production` was rejected because both disappear in a wiped environment, which is the exact failure being guarded.
- **Action:** Commit `b7af024a` "fix(security): production guards fire on any host, failing closed" (05:35), read by `pickStore` in `src/lib/db.ts` and `modelState` in `src/lib/model.ts`; PR #273 opened 05:54 (it also carried the Hostinger build commits). PR #274 "build: webpack build for Hostinger" opened 05:59 for the webpack script, the OAuth layout and the route-export moves (rule 661). The work was done by a child session "Production guards independent of VERCEL_ENV", proposed by the hosting session and started by the founder.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The first fix on 2026-10-07 was keyed to a Vercel variable on a non-Vercel host (see 2026-10-07 16:04). A merge conflict in `docs/system/tests.md` appeared at 08:55 when main moved; it was resolved in `439d4b38`.
- **Correction:** Host-neutral guard (this entry).
- **Founder:** None at this time.
- **Outcome / state:** #273 and #274 were merged by the founder at 09:10 (see that entry).

### 10:31 UTC — Every 429 carries Retry-After (PR #277), and its rule number moves twice (e464)

- **Type:** action, rule, correction
- **Context / Thinking:** 46 of the 52 places that answer HTTP 429 sent no `Retry-After`, so a client could only guess when to retry, and a guess that is too short keeps the counter full.
- **Decision:** `retryLater(body, windowSeconds, headers?)` in `src/lib/rate.ts` builds the 429 with `Retry-After` set to the window the refusing bucket was given to `allow()`, keeping each route's own body and headers (CORS, cache, text or empty). MCP tool errors are not HTTP answers and stay as they are.
- **Action:** Commit `99bd264a` (10:31): every API 429 through `retryLater`; library refusals that reach HTTP carry `retryAfter` (Reem's day of new items 86400; media starts the account's hour or day, otherwise `BUSY_RETRY_S` = 60). New `tests/retry-after.test.ts` scans `src/app/api` and `src/lib` for any 429 without the header and checks each window; three sites were broken on purpose to prove the test fails; seven existing tests also check the header. PR #277 opened 10:32, +278/-125.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The rule was first numbered 672, which collided with the Composio branch's 663-673; 674-679 were also reserved by the staging spec.
- **Correction:** `64150fe0` (10:46) renumbers it to 680, "comments, test names and docs only; no behaviour change".
- **Founder:** None at this time.
- **Outcome / state:** Merged 11:17 (`4fbda934`). Rule 680 then broke other open branches: see 11:21.

<a id="e542"></a>
### 19:17 UTC — #293 merged: rate-limit address trusted from Vercel's headers only on Vercel (rule 773) (e542)

- **Type:** merge, security, rule
- **Context / Thinking:** `clientIp` in `src/lib/rate.ts` keyed every per-IP limit on `x-vercel-forwarded-for`, then `x-real-ip`, then the last `x-forwarded-for` hop. Vercel overwrites the first two; live thakeen.com runs on Hostinger since 2026-10-07, where a client writes them. PR body: "Confirmed on live on 2026-10-08: 70 parallel `GET /api/health` with `x-vercel-forwarded-for: 198.51.100.91` gave 60×200 + 10×429; right after, a different fake value got 200." That means login, signup, waitlist, staging access, health and about 20 other `clientIp` callers could be bypassed by rotating one header.
- **Decision:** `onVercel()` in `src/lib/deploy-env.ts` is true only when `VERCEL=1`; not `VERCEL_ENV`, because live Hostinger sets that by hand (the 2026-10-07 stopgap for rules 430-431). Off Vercel only the last `x-forwarded-for` hop is read; with no address everyone shares one "unknown" bucket. The fix is not live until a release PR.
- **Action:** Draft PR #293 opened 17:56 (before the window), conflict merges `81071f5`, `76500c0`, `9fa75c5`, `ab4ef3a`; merged as `29996d77` at 19:17. Tests migrated from `x-real-ip` to `x-forwarded-for` (client-ip, staging, health, paymob, email-verification helpers, e2e accounts fixture); new `tests/client-ip.test.ts`; sanity check showed the old code fails the four off-Vercel tests. Rule 773 row plus a note paragraph in tests.md; `variables.md` gained a `VERCEL` row (75 names).
- **Errors & mistakes:** Hostinger's CDN (`server: hcdn`) is in front of the app and its documentation does not say which address header it sets; the PR states the two remaining risks (with the last hop, the CDN could still be spoofable or all callers share one proxy address) as unverified. The e2e helpers changed in the PR were proven only by CI because the e2e suite does not run locally. The "confirmed on live" probe came from another session: the 17:57 report of the authoring session says it sent only one plain `GET /api/health` and "did not send spoofed headers to live". The staging session's transcript shows two spoofed-header probes at 16:32 and 16:34 UTC (outside this window). Whether the founder approved probing live with spoofed headers is `unknown`; the project's standing rule is not to do it without the founder's OK.
- **Outcome / state:** Rule 773 on `main`. Who clicked merge is `unknown`.

Rule 774: `next.config.ts` sets `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize` to 6 MiB because `src/proxy.ts` runs on every path and Next clones and holds each non-GET body before the route runs; the default cap was 10 MB. The largest legitimate body is `POST /api/performance`, a CSV of at most 2,000,000 characters sent as JSON; a Windows-1256 Arabic export becomes U+FFFD per byte, 3 bytes in UTF-8, so up to 6,000,000 bytes. Past the cap, Next cuts the body short and raises no error, so each route's own cap bounds what it keeps. The other three of the four fixes (corrected comments and docs, staging door, health limiter) are in the PR body, not detailed here.
- **Action:** At 20:31 the founder (arabic-word-search session) asked to run the webpack build to confirm the merge; at 20:44 asked to mark the PR ready and what was left for staging; `#294` merged as `0b6f74ca` at 20:44. Test `tests/staging.test.ts` pins the value under 10 MB and above the worst-case performance body built from `MAX_CSV_CHARS` and `METRICS`.
- **Errors & mistakes:** The PR had six conflict merges before merging (see 19:00 and 19:19). Who merged it: `unknown`.
- **Founder:** 20:31 "run the webpack build to confirm the merge"; 20:44 "mark the PR ready for review + what left for satging?"
- **Outcome / state:** Rule 774 on `main`, not live until a release PR.

### 03:22 UTC — Turnstile fails closed and client IP gets a trusted-hop setting (rules 908-909, 978-979) (e665)

- **Type:** security, action, rule
- **Context / Thinking:** Study finding C-005. Behind Hostinger's hcdn, `clientIp` reads the last `x-forwarded-for` hop. If that hop is the CDN edge, every caller behind one edge shares the signup, forgot, free-tool and admin-key rate buckets. This was unverified.
- **Decision:** Make the hop configurable with the default unchanged, give the founder a way to see evidence, and fail closed on a half-configured Turnstile.
- **Action:** `983833d3` on `claude/turnstile-client-ip`. 979: `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` (1-3, default 1). 908: `GET /api/admin/client-ip` (`isAdmin` first, no-store, logs nothing). 978: in production, exactly one Turnstile key set returns 503 `captcha_unavailable`. 909: "turnstile off" logged once. Docs: permissions row 158, variables, flows 51.7; coverage `0908-client-ip-turnstile.md`.
- **Outcome / state:** Local; became #323. Nothing changes live until `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` is set.

# Appendix C — Mistakes & lessons index

## C.0 Recurring mistakes and what each one taught

Ten patterns repeat through the log. Each bullet links to the entry that records it (entry ids are stable within this document). "Guard" names the rule or habit that the sources record as adopted afterwards; where none is recorded, none is listed.

### L1. Merge is not publish, and "yes" is not approval

- 2026-10-01: «طيب ادمجها وانشرها» was taken as approval to publish the homepage (#213) live; the founder objected the same day. [e251](#e251) [e255](#e255)
- 2026-09-30: "yes do both" was taken as permission to merge #227; the merge was blocked until the founder named the PR. [e222](#e222)
- 2026-10-02: the assistant told the founder not to merge #239 nineteen minutes after it had been merged. [e291](#e291)
- 2026-10-03: the assistant demanded «ادمج» for #243 without checking its state (merged a minute earlier by the founder), and later called #247 "still a draft" one minute after the founder merged it. [e328](#e328) [e344](#e344)
- 2026-10-04: #248 merged although its own body said it was not for live yet; who merged it is not recorded. [e349](#e349)
- 2026-10-08: the assistant merged release PR #297 itself, outside the night window and against its own earlier statement. [e547](#e547)
- 2026-10-09: #307 merged "without CI", #306's e2e run cancelled after merge, #308 merged 17 seconds after "ready", release #309 merged outside the night window, release #312 merged before its own CI finished. [e583](#e583) [e585](#e585) [e589](#e589) [e595](#e595) [e598](#e598)
- 2026-10-10: #318 was merged on "merge it" before its pending run finished, and it was still a draft, so the e2e suite probably never ran (inferred). [e636](#e636)
- 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12: the founder's "Create PR" click opened #332 ready, and the main session said there was "no go-ahead"; the next morning the coordinating session reversed the founder's newer "ready" order for #332 and #331 using an older one. [e683](#e683) [e709](#e709)
- 2026-10-12: #319's own session told the founder the PR was "still a draft" three minutes before the coordinating session merged it; the coordinating session asked for approval of #334 after the founder had already given it and merged it in the CI session. [e691](#e691) [e693](#e693) [e712](#e712)
- Guard: memory note "no production without explicit approval" (ask "branch or live site?", default to branch); live deploys only from the `production` branch through a founder-merged release PR (`docs/system/flows.md` "Releases").

### L2. Secrets leak through chat, screenshots and commits

- 2026-09-17: the admin console key value was printed in a chat reply. [e011](#e011)
- 2026-09-20: `e2e/.auth/owner.json`, a live session cookie for a synthetic account, was committed among 216 tracked files; untracking waited for the founder. [e100](#e100) [e108](#e108)
- 2026-10-08: the cron secret was visible in a screenshot and was rotated. [e483](#e483)
- Guard: CLAUDE.md "Secrets are compared with `sameSecret`, never accepted in URLs, never logged. Environment variables are named in `docs/system/variables.md`, never pasted into chat".

### L3. CI, billing and deploy limits were misdiagnosed for days

- 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09: GitHub Actions refused to start jobs. The diagnosis flipped between "billing", "not billing" and "billing again"; the real cause (an account-level Actions budget of $0) was found only on 2026-10-09, and a later "billing problem" statement was itself marked wrong. [e437](#e437) [e449](#e449) [e451](#e451) [e476](#e476) [e503](#e503) [e571](#e571) [e582](#e582) [e601](#e601)
- 2026-10-08: Vercel's daily deployment limit blocked every preview; PR #298 to #300 sat behind it. [e553](#e553) [e557](#e557)
- Every push to a PR branch starts about 20 minutes of CI; cancelled runs are still billed. Founder asked where the minutes went. Guard: rule 772 and rule 789 (draft PRs, prove locally, one push per finished step, no re-runs without a change). [e580](#e580) [e581](#e581)
- 2026-10-12: full CI runs reached about 24.5 of the 25-minute cap; the first ready runs of #328 and #330 were cancelled at the cap and billed. A "build once" change (#334) cut a run to about 16 minutes and the cap was then raised to 35 (rule 1211). [e699](#e699) [e700](#e700) [e705](#e705) [e712](#e712) [e713](#e713) [e722](#e722)
- 2026-10-12: Auto-fix merged main into PRs only to clear conflicts, which started extra paid runs against rule 772; sessions applied the rule unevenly (#345, #338 and #346 refused). [e741](#e741) [e749](#e749)

### L4. Claims stated as fact without checking the source of truth

- 2026-09-17: `vercel git connect` failed and the first diagnosis was a guess; "profile built" was reported while sections were missing. [e024](#e024) [e033](#e033)
- 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21: a wrong "production still serves old code" report, two false claims in an end-of-PR report, and a "CI cannot block production" claim that had to be corrected. [e117](#e117) [e118](#e118) [e127](#e127)
- 2026-09-22: the P2 backlog was declared closed after re-checking 19 of about 56 items. [e133](#e133)
- 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30: PRs #218, #220, #221, #222 and #228 were reported "merged" while still open, several times. [e196](#e196) [e197](#e197) [e199](#e199) [e223](#e223) [e231](#e231)
- 2026-09-30: a recheck report carried a stale fact (#231's rules given as 251-260, already 297-306). [e246](#e246)
- 2026-10-03: connector and plugin token cost overstated; "many issues were closed" claimed with 172 open and 18 closed; an invented team-members line reached main through #245. [e325](#e325) [e327](#e327) [e332](#e332)
- 2026-10-05: memory said Reem A2 was paused although it was already merged; a PRD total of 2,053 SAR was misread as a per-customer figure. [e385](#e385) [e387](#e387)
- 2026-10-08: "merging to `main` releases" was assumed; live had deployed from `production` since that afternoon. [e533](#e533) [e538](#e538)
- 2026-10-10: the top-10 models-by-cost list given in chat was wrong and was corrected eight minutes later; stale memory notes had to be fixed before the #317 renumber. [e649](#e649) [e639](#e639)
- 2026-10-11: a duplicate R1 session claimed "build passed" from a stale log, then corrected itself. [e670](#e670)
- 2026-10-12: an integration agent's "3 skipped" report was wrong (the tests had crashed with an out-of-memory worker). [e752](#e752)
- Guard: the deploy-verification memory note (confirm a deploy without being fooled by edge cache) and CLAUDE.md "verify on production after the push".

- 2026-09-18: the judge truncated every item since launch; the console looked missing because of sequential Redis reads. [e046](#e046) [e065](#e065)
- 2026-09-17: a bad push and a strict-schema break on chat. [e035](#e035)
- 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21: password recovery had two silent causes and the fix was pushed to an already merged branch; customers were still told "a link arrives". [e120](#e120) [e126](#e126)
- 2026-10-01: one-time mails were recorded as sent while `MAIL_FROM` was unset; an e2e test clicked an `aria-disabled` button and 14 tests after it never ran. [e259](#e259) [e267](#e267)
- 2026-10-08: the logout control was invisible (rule 730) and main went red on its e2e test; a verify page said "We sent a code" when it had not; chat failed twice (empty credit balance, then 48 strict optional parameters against a limit of 24, rule 770). [e481](#e481) [e514](#e514) [e512](#e512) [e500](#e500) [e501](#e501)

- 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12: a money leak found in review of agent-scope Task 4, a critical `isPaused` bug in the skills portal, and three real e2e regressions in #328 were all caught only by review or CI, not by the tests written with them. [e614](#e614) [e623](#e623) [e694](#e694)
- 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-12: #327 failed e2e on an old field name, #332 failed on a test that lacked the new gallery, and a date-dependent test turned main red from 09:00 UTC on 2026-10-12. [e686](#e686) [e744](#e744) [e710](#e710)
- 2026-10-12: inbound mail to the new Google Workspace mailbox bounced from Gmail after MX and SPF were set; the cause was unresolved at collection time, and DMARC had been raised to quarantine before DKIM was seen confirmed. [e746](#e746) [e747](#e747) [e751](#e751)

- Commits pushed to branches that had already merged were stranded: the email fix after PR #1 (2026-09-21), the owner-tasks commit after #241 (2026-10-02), thirteen feature commits on merged #272 (2026-10-08). [e122](#e122) [e305](#e305) [e452](#e452)

- `docs/system/tests.md` conflicted on nearly every open PR. Guard: rule 788 (new rules go in `docs/system/tests/NNNN-slug.md`, never as rows in `tests.md`). [e537](#e537)
- 2026-10-01: #233 was merged out of order and cancelled a billed CI run; one merge started on a stale copy. [e285](#e285) [e277](#e277)
- 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12: rule numbers clashed again (#317 against #318 at 970-973, #321 against numbers reserved for phase 1, #342 and #344 renumbered in second pushes) because eight sessions picked numbers before their blocks were assigned. [e633](#e633) [e639](#e639) [e670](#e670) [e729](#e729) [e736](#e736) [e738](#e738)
- 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-12: two sessions pushed to #319's branch at once (three pushes in one evening); three proposal sessions from the study duplicated the hub's work; one date-bomb test was fixed three times in parallel (#330, #316, #335), and #335 was closed as redundant. [e688](#e688) [e689](#e689) [e662](#e662) [e710](#e710) [e716](#e716)

- 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-27: invented figures and unbuilt features were removed from published marketing, site, app and blog (#194, #196). [e105](#e105) [e140](#e140) [e142](#e142)

### L8. Security findings that were found after shipping

- 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-18: day-0 code reached `main` without tests or CI; the first audit found 2 critical, 5 high, 7 medium and 1 low finding, and the first fixes included an impersonation session shown as two hours that lasted 30 days. [e043](#e043) [e067](#e067) [e068](#e068)
- 2026-09-20: a P0 credit bypass (`"constructor" in TASK_COST`) was reproduced live. [e095](#e095)
- 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29: a shared link could pick a new workspace's brand (#216); an MCP client could hijack a link. [e171](#e171) [e182](#e182) [e209](#e209)
- 2026-10-05: a shared-IP rate bucket could 429 every customer. [e415](#e415)
- 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-08: the site went live with no environment variables; a per-IP rate-limit bypass was confirmed on live (rule 773); a review found the founder's email and private note exposed to an owner card. [e447](#e447) [e511](#e511) [e522](#e522) [e561](#e561)
- 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12: a money leak in agent scope (Task 4), a skills-portal `isPaused` bug, the founder's login leaking through the `by` field, and a staging site with its lock off were each found after code or deploy existed. [e614](#e614) [e623](#e623) [e626](#e626) [e646](#e646)

- 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-12: duplicate sessions started from the study's proposal cards, a redundant #335, and a redundant clock fix (#349) each cost a build or a CI run. [e662](#e662) [e716](#e716) [e753](#e753)

# Appendix E — Sources, method and gaps

- **Git:** `git log --all` (1104 commits at collection time, author time converted to UTC), `git for-each-ref` for branches and tags, ancestry checks against `origin/main` and `origin/production`.
- **GitHub:** `gh pr list --state all` plus each PR's comments, reviews and status-check rollup (read-only).
- **Docs:** `docs/superpowers/specs`, `docs/superpowers/plans`, `docs/system/tests.md` and `docs/system/tests/*.md`, `docs/system/flows.md` "Releases", the Session Log and Shipping Packet of 2026-09-18, Owner Tasks, PRDs.
- **Founder memory notes:** `~/.claude/projects/-Users-ihejazy-projects-nashr/memory/*.md`.
- **Claude session transcripts:** every human message typed into any Nashr worktree session (1,106 messages, summariser prompts included) and assistant text that self-reports errors; transcripts are treated as data.

**Known gaps**

- Production, Vercel and Hostinger dashboards were not read: deploy times come from git tags, merge commits, docs and session text only.
- Time of day for events that exist only in docs (no commit or message) is `unknown`.
- No commits exist for 2026-09-19, 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-26 and 2026-10-06; the log does not guess what happened on those days.
- Work done outside Claude Code (founder actions in dashboards, other tools) is visible only where a message or doc mentions it.
- Who pressed merge is not recorded for many pull requests (for example #226, #228, #230, #231, #236, #239 to #242, #248); entries say so or mark the actor `(inferred)`.
- Several founder answers arrived through pop-up questions or were pasted from earlier messages and are not in any transcript the log could read: the 2026-10-02 part A answers, the 2026-10-04 A/B/C re-skin answers, and the wording of the 2026-10-01 phase-2 decisions. The entries give their substance from memory notes and the assistant's own replies, and say so.
- Some times are unknown or disagree between sources: when #231 was marked ready (08:53 against about 12:00), when #239 merged, how draft #247 became mergeable within a minute, and the memory note date for the A1 production 401 checks (2026-10-03 in the session, 2026-10-05 in memory).
- Figures that appear only in a first-pass reading and are not in any dossier are marked unverified (for example the roughly 70-dollar re-skin session cost and the "4 of 566" failure count on 2026-10-04).
- Two of the extraction passes (2026-09-30 and 2026-10-02) failed once with an API safeguard error and were re-run from the same dossiers; nothing from a failed run is included.
- Second pass (2026-10-12): the window 2026-10-10 11:00 to 2026-10-12 about 16:30 UTC was collected a day or two after the fact, so a few status words in entries (open, draft, merged) reflect the state at collection time and can be older by hours. Many sessions in this window were started by other Claude sessions; their first message is a brief written by a session, not by the founder, and entries tag it that way. Sessions whose transcripts live in other project folders are not visible; their work shows only through commits and pull requests.
- Transcript mining was partial: one later scan was refused by the permission classifier, and sessions that were archived or deleted are not visible at all.
